summary: Teams analyze a case study and data pack for an AI-assisted EdTech SaaS company, using AI tools to create professional deliverables in Finance, IT, Business/Marketing, and Digital Media Design. Teams submit a combined PDF with all artifacts, an AI Use Log, and required forms, then present their integrated AI solution virtually to judges. The event emphasizes ethical, responsible, and reproducible AI use, and includes both a technical project and a live presentation.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges' questions
submission_requirements: Submit all artifacts, Works Cited, AI Use Log, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form in one combined PDF file to https://upload.bpa.org no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on January 15, 2027.
Artifacts 1, 2, and 3 each comply with the two-page limit and follow the report format in the Style & Reference Manual.
Digital Media Design Artifact follows its own format and is not subject to the two-page limit.
Works Cited page is excluded from the two-page count for Artifacts 1, 2, and 3.

Header information on the first page of the report should be as follows: Contestant ID Number (Sender’s ID Number - XXXXXXXX), Edna Renick (Recipient’s Name), Administrative Support Department (Recipient’s Department), and Current Date.
Team ID is required for all submissions.
Materials from non-registered members and/or those missing team ID cannot be accepted.
The team is responsible for securing a BPA Release Form(s) from any person, including themselves, whose image or work is used in the project.
The team is responsible for citing all sources, including themselves and any AI tools used, on the Works Cited page for any work used on the project.
In-text citations are required throughout all papers.
Materials must follow the organization's BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization's name.
deadlines: The registration deadline is no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, on December 1, 2026
National Deadline: January 15, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
competencies: Demonstrate understanding of AI concepts, capabilities, and limitations
Apply AI tools to finance, IT operations, marketing, and digital media design
Use structured case study data to drive evidence-based decisions
Design AI workflows and prompts that are structured and reproducible
Demonstrate ethical and responsible AI use, including bias mitigation, transparency, data privacy, and security
Communicate complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders
Produce professional written, visual, and strategic deliverables
Demonstrate teamwork, project management, and decision-making skills
Apply principles of design and rules for proper layout in developing business publications for multiple screens and printing situations
Use principles of design, layout, and typography in media and user experience design
Demonstrate effective persuasive and informative communication and presentation skills

judging_notes: Judges' comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level.
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC.
eligibility_notes: Any middle level, secondary, or postsecondary contestant may enter this event.
A team will consist of 2–4 contestants.
There are no restrictions on the number of entries per chapter or per state.

Teams who do not submit an entry following the topic listed below or do not follow the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified.
Teams participating in the competition must be registered for the event prior to the submission deadline to be eligible.
